recommend.description: proceed: nothing derivable blocks it. amend: a derivable defect in the record. recut: the decomposition does not hold. resurvey: the premise is wrong, not the commitment. ask: stop for a person — the repair is a decision the record may not make for itself (scope, what the intent means, worth at this cost), and an amender would settle it by guessing.

checks.description: The four derivations, each with what you found. Never empty.

status.description: underivable means you could NOT derive this check — a missing yardstick, not a failed one. Never use broken for something you could not check.

findings.description: Empty when recommending proceed; may be empty when recommending ask. Every entry must cite what it falsifies.

claim-id.description: The id of the design claim this finding is about — the slug shown in brackets, WITHOUT the brackets. Empty string when the finding is about no single claim, or the design lists invariants with no ids.

check.description: The derived check this finding shows broken. Empty string when it bears on none of the four.

confirmed.description: Every claim you were asked to check that you went and checked and found to hold, each with where you read it and whether the code you read already makes it true. By id, not by sentence. Empty when the design lists invariants with no ids.

id.description: The bracketed slug, without the brackets.

evidence.description: The file:line references you read that show it holds. Never empty: a confirmation citing nothing is not counted.

at_this_tree.description: holds: the code you read already makes the claim true. owed: the claim is a sound commitment, and the code you read does not meet it yet — the build has to make it true.

unchecked.description: Each subject you were asked to check and COULD NOT check here, with why — its evidence is not in the code (production data, a deploy history, a service you cannot reach). A subject listed here is ruled on, visibly unconfirmed. Not for a subject you simply did not get to: that one you go and check.

id.description: The bracketed slug, without the brackets.

relation_rulings.description: One ruling per baseline id listed under relation-honest — every one of them, and nothing else. Empty only when the prompt lists none.

id.description: The baseline id as listed, without the brackets.

cause.description: Empty unless the prompt shows a previous ruling on this id and this ruling differs from it. Then: what moved since that ruling and makes it wrong — in the record, in the code, or in an objection shown to you. A reversal with no cause, on an id whose record did not move, is not taken.

ruling.description: breaks: this design stops the id being true of the area, so it belongs under :breaks. stands: it is still true once this design is built.

reason.description: Why — for stands, what keeps it true; for breaks, what in the design moves it.

asks.description: The question the human still has to answer, with everything derived taken off the table. Required whatever you recommend. Never answer it yourself.
